name: What is the difference between wet insulation and insulation damaged by a small leak?

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between wet insulation and insulation damaged by a small leak?

acceptedAnswer.text: While both involve water, the difference often lies in the extent and duration of moisture exposure. Wet insulation typically refers to insulation that has absorbed a significant amount of water, often from a larger or ongoing leak, leading to saturation. Insulation damaged by a small leak might only have localized dampness, but if left unaddressed, even a small, consistent leak can lead to widespread wet insulation over time. Regardless of the size, any water intrusion into insulation warrants attention to prevent mold and structural issues.
acceptedAnswer.description: Wet insulation means saturated insulation, often from significant water. Insulation damaged by a small leak may be localized, but still requires attention to prevent further issues.
